title: An End-to-End Automated Pipeline for Controllable Crack Data Synthesis
mechanism: Procedural Bezier skeletons turned into crack masks by a GAN, rendered by dual-ControlNet Stable Diffusion; an ensemble of real-trained segmenters assigns pixel-wise label confidence that weights the synthetic loss instead of hard filtering; detectors evaluated by probability of detection (POD) vs crack width.
adaptation: Use the existing 5-seed house ensemble as the confidence model for any synthetic crack pair (it already sits at relF1@2 0.897); weight synthetic pixels by agreement with the inherited mask. Add POD vs crack width and contrast (a90/95) to the benchmark, computed on test and E1 crack components.
min_experiment: Arm: row-1 synthetic stream with confidence-weighted loss. Baseline: same stream unweighted, both on PF, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 relF1@2 and test crack relP@2. Kill: gain < +0.01 on both.
evidence: R: improves five segmentation networks over conventional, diffusion and flow-matching augmentation on CRACK500 and CrackTree200; confidence weighting beats threshold filtering at every threshold; U-Net width detected at 90% POD / 95% confidence 8.0 -> 4.3 px; ECE 14.2% -> 9.6%.

alt_notes.adaptation: Take only the confidence weighting: the house 5-seed ensemble scores every pasted or rendered pixel, and that score weights the loss in the copy-paste, ObjectAug and procedural arms. For the benchmark, report POD against crack contrast and length on test and E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Any synthetic arm with vs without ensemble-confidence weights, 5 seeds. Metric: that arm's main metric. Kill if gain < +0.01.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use only the confidence weighting: house 5-seed ensemble scores every pasted, carved or rendered pixel in the CarveMix, Soft-CP, Synth4Seg and procedural arms. For the benchmark, report POD vs crack contrast and length on test and E1.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Best synthetic arm with vs without ensemble-confidence weights; that arm's main metric. Kill: < +0.01.
